summary: The what's-new feed now refreshes every 15 minutes instead of every 30
A failed login now shows why it failed instead of "Request failed (401)"
A rejected login no longer reveals whether the username exists
Nodes are listed by hostname again instead of their internal identity UUID
Modpacks now appears in the navbar and in Settings -> Modules once the feature is enabled
Modpacks split into two switches: the subsystem for admins, plus "open authoring to users"
A per-user modpack permission set by hand is now marked as an override and survives the platform switch
The modpack on/off switch no longer exists twice: Settings -> Features owns it, Settings -> Modpacks owns storage
What's new is a modal now, with the latest update on top and the history below it
The what's-new icon stays highlighted while entries exist and only greys out when there is nothing to show
A rejected 2FA setup code is now logged with the reason: clock drift (and by how much) or a code from an older secret
The 2FA wizard explains a rejected code and offers "start over with a new QR"
The disk-quota warning now names the fix (pquota / prjquota) instead of only the problem
Warp: "when the limit is reached" is now settable for multi-connection keys too, not just fixed ones
Warp: inline help for policy, max connections and how external nodes relate to Infrastructure -> Nodes
The sidebar's "New Container" is now a "+" menu that says what you can create and why not
New "My nodes" page: connect your own machine, manage enrollment keys, see its status
Settings -> Users -> Billing shows what a tenant may use and can grant BYON or route-only for N days
The server Reload button is gone; a full Restart is the reliable way to re-read plugins and config
Tickets and Modpacks open their real pages instead of an empty "coming soon" placeholder
The Modpacks module row is re-derived from the feature flags on every start, so it stops showing "Admin" after authoring was opened
Username history moved into Edit Profile, and My Modpacks left the profile menu now that Modpacks has its own navbar entry
The Beam force-update floor now always comes from the signed release manifest; the manual field is gone
The Beam prerelease (dev) update channel was removed; everyone is on the one release stream
DNS now supports 13 providers - Cloudflare, Hetzner, deSEC, IONOS, GoDaddy, Gandi, Bunny, Porkbun, netcup, Namecheap, ClouDNS, OVH and Route 53
Providers that need more than an API token now get the right inputs instead of one box labelled "API Token"
S3 buckets and credentials are defined once under Settings -> Storage Connections; Core Storage, Modpacks and Backups reference one instead of asking again
Settings -> Modpacks can fill in Core's public address from the one you are reached on, instead of you retyping it
Settings -> Nodes now states both ways a machine becomes a node; the old card claimed no manual setup was needed, which stopped being true with the pairing hardening
Settings -> Nodes split: Nodes is the connected list, Node settings holds admission and enroll tokens
Adding a route: subdomain and custom domain are one switch now, so the custom-domain half is findable
My nodes rebuilt: bring-your-own-node and route-only as separate cards, each with its usage against your plan and the deploy stack plus commands
The read-only demo is reachable at /login?demo=1, so a link can drop someone straight into the panel with no account
After connecting a store account the browser is sent back to the panel; needs FRONTEND_URL set, otherwise no link is offered
What's new groups by component: the latest update on top, then everything Core, Panel or Node changed under its own heading instead of in arrival order
Each component is now measured against its OWN installed build, so updating Core while leaving the nodes alone no longer reports the node's changes as installed
The node reports which update-feed position its image was built at, so the panel can tell whether the node specifically is behind
